gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a security camera inside a feeder case like the Wasserstein sits closer to the birds than its lens can focus: Digital Camera World tested the case with a Ring Stick Up Cam, found the birds were 'closer than the Ring's nearest focusing distance', and listed 'Security cameras can't focus closely enough' as a con.
standout_why: Reviewed.com (cited, 2026-11-06) never mentions minimum focus distance or motion-sensor type. Its only Wasserstein mention is a build-quality comparison, and Blink, Ring and Wyze come up only in a privacy aside. The Digital Camera World buying guide (rank 5, uncited) covers only all-in-one feeders, and the part I could read never mentions Ring, Blink, Wyze, focus or the Wasserstein case. WIRED (cited) blocked my fetch, so I could not check it; that is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: This hits the 'feeder for my own camera' half of ChatGPT's answer. The Wasserstein case puts the Blink, Ring or Wyze camera at a fixed spot just behind the tray, and two named reviewers found that the nearest birds were either out of focus (DCW, Ring) or in a blind spot or 'too close to identify' (Bob Vila, Ring). Blink itself says its PIR detection works best at 7–19 ft. A clip-on bird camera like the Birdfy Cam 2 4K or Cam 2K sits on a separate arm, so you can move it back from the feeder. Motion sensing does not separate the two: Birdfy's own spec sheet lists the Cam 2 4K as PIR too. This supports making a dedicated feeder camera the pick for sharp bird close-ups. The case stays the budget choice for someone who already owns a camera and accepts softer images.

findings.label: Close-focus result with a security camera inside the case
findings.value: Birds were 'closer than the Ring's nearest focusing distance'; the reviewer could not get 'a completely crisp image of birds'; listed con: 'Security cameras can't focus closely enough'
findings.source_title: Wasserstein Bird Feeder Smart Case review: Bird watching made easy? (Digital Camera World, Adam Juniper, 2023-04-04)
findings.note: Hands-on test with a Ring Stick Up Cam, not a Blink Outdoor 4. The case holds every compatible camera at the same distance from the tray, so the problem very likely applies to the others, but the Blink Outdoor 4 was not tested.

findings.label: Birds nearest the camera
findings.value: 'Those feeding closest to the camera were either in a blind spot outside the field of view or were too close to identify'; rated 7.8/10
findings.source_title: Wasserstein Bird Feeder Smart Camera Case review (Bob Vila, Mark Wolfe, 2023-05-19)
findings.note: Tested with a Ring Stick Up HD. Also says that in the wall and tree setups the case must be taken off the mount to reach the camera.

findings.label: Motion-detection mechanism and best range
findings.value: PIR (passive infrared) sensor that 'detects heat energy'; 'Blink cameras detect motion best from about 7 to 19 feet (2m to 6m) away'; 'Objects that are the same apparent temperature as the background may not be detected'
findings.note: Blink lists the Outdoor 4 among its PIR models; the Mini and Mini 2 use pixel comparison instead. A camera in the feeder case sits much closer than 7 ft to the birds.

findings.label: Motion detection and video modes
findings.value: Motion detection: 'Passive infrared sensor'; 3840×2160 at 20 fps, 1920×1080 at 60 fps, 1280×720 at 120 fps; 9,000 mAh; 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi; IP66; no microSD
findings.note: PIR as well, so the sensor type does not separate it from Blink. The difference is placement: it sits on its own arm rather than in a fixed slot behind the tray.

findings.label: Motion detection (original Birdfy Cam spec sheet)
findings.value: Motion detection: 'Passive infrared sensor'; 2304×1296 at 20 fps or 1080p at 30 fps; 5,200 mAh; 2.4 GHz only; IP65
findings.note: This page is titled 'Birdfy Cam'. Its specs (5,200 mAh, 2.4 GHz, 2K at 20 fps) match our Cam 2K row, but the page does not name it as the Cam 2K.
